thread:
maria: Heads-up — observed a tenant request where header-driven alias X-Model: redwood-chat-latest-v2 resolved, but the gateway routed to a cpu-safe quantized variant and then the request was throttled by per-model quota. This looked like a mismatch between routing resolution and runtime compatibility checks. Anyone seen this pattern?

samir: Ugh. Can you paste the exact request headers and the routing rule that matched? Trying to see whether the gateway applied an override or whether runtime fell back.

maria: Paste below. Request headers: `X-Model: redwood-chat-latest-v2`, `X-Tenant: acme-inc`, `X-Route: payment-inference`. Gateway matched route rule id `route:acme/payment` which has `alias: chat-latest`. Runtime log: `selected_variant=chat-latest-quantized-cpu` with compat flag `quantized=true cpu_only=true`.

Here's the routing snippet from the route config (simplified):
```yaml
match:
  path: "/v1/generate"
  headers:
    X-Tenant: "acme-inc"
    X-Route: "payment-inference"
actions:
  - select_alias: chat-latest
  - allow_fallback: true
```

alex: Thanks. Two things jumping out: 1) alias -> variant resolution should be compatibility-aware *before* quota decision; otherwise we charge/throttle wrong quota buckets. 2) We need a deterministic precedence for overrides: explicit route pins / tenant pins > header alias > global alias > fallback.

kai: UX/console note: when a route alias causes a variant downgrade due to compatibility, show a yellow warning on the route config page and surface the candidate variant and why it was chosen (compat + runtime-capacity). Right now console only shows alias->alias mapping, not resolved variant.

samir: Agree on precedence. Current implementation does: resolve alias -> pick best runtime-compatible variant at runtime (which is fine) but we were recording quota against the alias id, not the resolved variant id. That made the quota lookup fail because the quantized-CPU variant has a different quota bucket. Fix will require using the final resolved model id for quota checks and telemetry tagging.

maria: Also saw another oddity: when `allow_fallback: true` is set, the gateway will try fallback variants across regions which sometimes bypass region-specific quotas. Should be explicit about regional scope when allowing fallback.

alex: Proposed short-term actions: (1) change quota check to use resolved model id (owner: @samir) (2) add warning in console when route alias resolution can lead to variant downgrade (owner: @kai) (3) add a telemetry gauge for alias->variant mismatches per-tenant (owner: @maria).

samir: I'll open a PR for quota resolution change — plan: add guard in gateway before decrementing quota: `quota_key = resolved_model_id || alias_id` and ensure motif. Target: today EOD for a hotfix, followed by tests that simulate alias->variant mapping.

kai: I'll add a console UX card — UX will show: "Resolved variant: chat-latest-quantized-cpu (downgrade due to cpu-only runtime)" and a link to rollout controls. Will mock tomorrow.

maria: I'll collect 10 sample traces (headers + route decision + runtime variant) and send to the PR. Also adding a small dashboard query: `sum(alias_to_variant_mismatch) by (tenant, route)` for immediate alerting.

deploy-bot: deploy started: gateway-v2.14.3 (hotfix/quota-resolve) for canary -> 3 hosts.

samir: Quick note on compatibility constraints: we should extend our model metadata with a `quota_bucket` attribute so resolution is straightforward and stable across renames/aliases. Will add to model catalog schema proposal in the PR.

alex: Long-term: consider adding explicit route policy field `enforce_variant_quota: true|false` and a console toggle for safety. Also update routing docs to call out precedence.

maria: Sounds good. If PR goes green and canary looks fine, we should patch prod today and then follow up with console + docs next week. Thanks all :thumbsup:

samir: cc @eng-sre for watch — I'll post the canary telemetry once deploy finishes.
